messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

**Chat for teams that ship code, not just talk about it**

Most chat apps treat engineers like every other department: ping, share a file, add a reaction. But your team reviews pull requests and gets paged at 2am, and the tool they live in all day should reflect that.

[Product] plugs into your stack. Push a commit and the channel shows the diff. Open an incident and the on-call schedule shows up automatically. Link a Jira ticket and its status updates in both places, so nobody digs through three tools to find where a task stands.

Threads hold up at scale. A channel with 40 engineers doesn't turn into noise — replies nest correctly, and search finds the message you're actually looking for, not just the one with the most reactions.

Notifications respect focus time. Engineers set working hours once, and the app holds non-urgent messages until they're back, while pages and @here alerts still get through. Fewer pings, and the ones that land matter.

For you, that means less time asking "did anyone see this?" and more time on decisions that need you. Admin controls show you what's happening across channels without reading every message, and audit logs cover the compliance questions your security team will eventually ask.

Moving from Slack or Teams takes a day, not a quarter: we bring over history, channels, and permissions, so your team doesn't lose its habits along with its old tool.

Try it with your team for 14 days. No credit card. No sales call.

**Chat built for people who ship code**

Most chat tools treat engineers like everyone else in the building: ping, share a file, react. Your team reviews pull requests and gets paged at 2am. The tool they live in should reflect that.

[Product] connects to your stack. Push a commit and the channel shows the diff. Open an incident and the on-call schedule appears automatically. Link a Jira ticket and its status stays in sync in both places — nobody hunts across three tools to find where a task stands.

Threads scale with the team. A channel with 40 engineers doesn't collapse into noise: replies nest where they belong, and search surfaces the message you need, not just the one with the most reactions.

Notifications respect focus time. Engineers set working hours once, and everything non-urgent waits until they're back — while pages and @here alerts still get through. Fewer interruptions, and the ones that land are the ones that matter.

For you, that means less time asking "did anyone see this?" and more time on the calls only you can make. Admin controls show what's happening across channels without reading every message, and audit logs cover the compliance questions your security team will eventually ask.

Switching from Slack or Teams takes a day, not a quarter. We migrate history, channels, and permissions, so your team keeps its habits along with its new tool.

Try it with your team for 14 days. No credit card, no sales call.
